intro: Competitions, results, injuries and the language of the sports pages.

The verb is «empatar». «Un empate a cero» is 0-0.
The stress is on «TO»: bik-TO-rya. The opposite is «la derrota».
The rr is strong: de-RRO-ta. «Sufrir una derrota» is to lose.
The c becomes z before o: «venzo». You say «vencer a un rival».
The verb is «lesionarse»: «se lesionó el tobillo». It has an accent: le-SIÓN.
It comes from «entrenar». Feminine: «la entrenadora».
With «a» it is a fan: «aficionado al fútbol». After a noun it is amateur: «pintor aficionado».
The ll sounds like y: me-DA-ya. There are gold, silver and bronze medals.
You beat a record. It also means to whisk: «batir huevos».
It has an accent: ÁR-bi-tro. In football he is also called «el colegiado».

texto:
**Competitions.** The **liga** lasts the whole season; the cup is a knockout. A **campeonato** has rounds: in each **eliminatoria** one loses and is out. The team that wins **se clasifica** (qualifies) for the next.

**Results.** You can win, lose or draw. The nouns are **victoria**, **derrota** and **empate**. Newspapers say **vencer** a rival.

**Prizes.** To finish champion or runner-up, win a **medalla** of gold, silver or bronze, **batir** a record, stand on the podium.

**People.** The **entrenador**, the **árbitro**, the captain, the rival and the **aficionados**.

**The body.** You train and warm up. When an athlete suffers a **lesión**, he gets injured. At the end of a career, he retires.

**Journalists' trick.** To avoid repeating, they say «el técnico» (the coach), «el colegiado» (the referee) or «el choque» (the match).

**Who wins.** Use **ganar**, **perder**, **empatar** and, in newspapers, **vencer a** a rival.

**The score.** The winner takes **por** and the two numbers are joined with **a**: **ganaron por dos a uno**. A draw takes only **a**: **empataron a cero**.

**The place.** With **quedar** + place or title: **quedar tercera**, **quedar campeón**. Also: **clasificarse para** the final.
